topics.topic: Exact representations, units, precision, and overflow rules for monotonic and UTC clock readings
questions: In what representation are monotonic readings and deadlines held and compared: integer ticks, integer nanoseconds, floating-point seconds, timedeltas from an origin, or another specified form, and with what precision and overflow rules?

What exact code representation and precision must every recorded UTC instant use outside A18, including whether it is a timezone-aware datetime, an epoch value, or text and whether sub-microsecond readings are rounded, truncated, or rejected?
In what exact type, unit and precision are monotonic readings represented and compared?
What exact representations, units and precision does `clock` return for its monotonic reading and its UTC wall-clock reading?

quotes:
Every duration in this decision — the 8 hours, the 30, 15 and 10
   minutes, the 60 seconds — is measured by the process's monotonic clock,
   which a change of the wall clock does not move and which counts the time
   the host or its VM was suspended, so a session does not outlive a
   suspension; instants Registry records
   and the 03:00 of A18 are UTC wall-clock time. Both readings reach the code
   through `clock` alone, emitted from the `system_clock_backend` IR whose
   `time_source_policy` the data closure declares (SPEC_STANDARD §6.8).

An owner session is never
   recorded (M11), so its instants — when it began, its last request, when
   its confirmation was shown — and its expiry at the latest are held as
   readings of that monotonic clock, and only they decide its limits; the
   UTC rule for recorded times does not reach them.
judgement.why: Exact runtime types, overflow behavior, and representation-level precision are field-type and format details owned by State 6; State 2 fixes the two sources and their semantics.

topics.topic: Number and sharing of UTC readings for publish and withdrawal timestamps
questions: Does one publish take one UTC reading shared by the new pointer's published instant and the previous pointer's superseded instant, or may those instants come from separate readings; likewise, how many readings does a withdrawal take?
Does one publish use one UTC reading for both the old pointer's superseded instant and the new pointer's published instant, or a separate reading for each?
Does one publish take one UTC wall-clock reading shared by the old pointer's superseded instant and the new pointer's published instant, or a separate reading for each?

quotes:
Publishing a pointer assigns its version, marks the type's published
   pointer `superseded` with its instant, and stores the new pointer
   `published` — all in one transaction, or none of it (R0-17, R0-35).
judgement.why: This is the same shared-versus-separate publish clock-reading question as P14, and the quoted timing passage has not changed.

topics.topic: Number, timing, and reuse of clock readings across session operations, expiry, and throttling
questions: For each sign-in, owner request, confirmation display, expiry pass and sign-in-throttling decision, how many monotonic and UTC readings are taken, and which fields and comparisons must share one reading?
For each sign-in and owner request, how many monotonic and UTC readings are taken, at which step are they taken, and which fields and checks must reuse the same reading?
Does one expiry pass take one monotonic reading for every session, or a new reading after each session's locks are acquired?
Is `now` captured once for an entire sign-in attempt and reused for pruning, lockout checking and recording a refusal, or may those checks read the monotonic clock separately?

quotes:
A new owner session (M11) with its sign-in reading of
`clock.monotonic_reading`, no pending confirmation and no uploaded file; the
refusal count cleared. A refused sign-in outside a lockout counts at its
reading; the fifth less than 15 minutes old starts a 15-minute lockout.

At its arrival a request carrying a valid session restarts the session's
30 minutes, whatever its answer — a CSRF refusal included; of concurrent
arrivals the latest counts (A13 rule 2). A sign-out's admission marks the
session signed out at once.

The session's pending confirmation is replaced: a new value from
`random_values.make_secret_value`, bound to the action, its target, what the
step showed and the digest of its inputs in a fixed order, and the reading
of `clock.monotonic_reading` it was shown at.

The pass alone
ends sessions by their limits: it takes the import lock, reads
`clock.monotonic_reading` once, and decides every session by that one
reading, in the order of their sign-in, each under its own lock, so the
order decides nothing.
judgement.why: State 5 assigns one reading to a sign-in attempt, an arrival, and a confirmation display, and explicitly requires one shared reading for the whole expiry pass.

topics.topic: Single accepted-import instant and which created records must share it
questions: What is the import's single instant, when is it read, and must every new Customer, the MigrationClosure and the import AuditEntry use exactly that same UTC reading?
How many UTC readings does the import take for newly created Customers, the migration closure and the audit entry, and must all of those records carry the same import instant?

How many UTC wall-clock readings does an accepted import take for the created instants of new Customers, the closure's success instant and the audit entry's instant, and which of those instants must be equal?

quotes:
An action has one instant: `operations` reads it from
  `clock.recorded_now` once, when the action's transaction begins, with
  today's date (`clock.today_in_utc`), and hands both to every module the
  action records a new instant or compares a date in. The import's records
  keep the instants their source holds ("Revisions and times"); the Customers
  it makes, its closure and its entry carry the action's one instant.
judgement.why: State 3 explicitly makes the import's Customers, closure, and audit entry share the one action instant read when its transaction begins.

completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs or waits (A13
rule 2).
